# MDL108 · `bracket-state-leak`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

mydumper's pre-processor mis-handles a line because an earlier line contains `[`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | loading |
| Default severity | error |
| Fix | safe |
| Flags | unsuppressible |
| Design references | P1, cases 12, 13, 16, 37, 48, 58 |

## Why

mydumper's config pre-processor appends `= 1` to lines that contain no `=`. When it meets a `[`, it copies the rest of the line verbatim and does not reset its state at the end of that line. The next line inherits a stale state:

- after a line with text before `[` (`# see [docs]`, an indented `  [mydumper]`, `key[fr]=v`), an empty line becomes `= 1`, a key/value pair with an empty key;
- after a line with `=` before `[` (`regex=^(a[bc])`), a flag such as `routines` gets no `= 1` and is not a key/value pair;
- on the line itself, a line without `=` that contains `[` (`; see [docs]`, `routines # [x]`) never gets its `= 1` either.

In every case GLib rejects the file and mydumper ignores all of it. The leak even crosses a valid `[group]` header placed in between.

## Example

❌ Before:

```ini
[mydumper]
routines=1
#[`db`.`t`]

[myloader]
```

```text
4:1-4:1 error MDL108[bracket-state-leak] mydumper's pre-processor turns this empty line into `= 1` because line 3 contains `[` after other text (GLib: Key file contains line “= 1” which is not a key-value pair, group, or comment)
  = mydumper ignores this entire file: it only logs a WARNING ("Failed to load config file") and runs with its defaults, exit code 0.
  note 3:1-3:12: mydumper's pre-processor does not reset its state after this line, because it contains `[`
  fix (safe): Remove the empty line
```

✅ After `mydumper-lint check --fix`:

```ini
[mydumper]
routines=1
#[`db`.`t`]
[myloader]
```

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL108: warning   # or error, info, off
```

Its diagnostics mean mydumper ignores the whole file: they cannot be suppressed by comments, only by the configuration or `--ignore`.
